messages.author: bd61fed06b4f0759
messages.subject: Different measurement invariance results from lavaan and Mplus7
parts:
Hi,

I ran a measurement inavariance analysis on a single factor model with eight categorical indicators across four groups using lavaan and Mplus7. I used "Model= configural metric scalar" feature of Mplus. Results from Mplus are as below:


                       Number of                         Degrees of
     Model        Parameters      Chi-square    Freedom     P-value

     Configural        96           3431.392            80       0.0000  (CFI=0.996,RMSEA= 0.103)
     Metric            75           3008.582            101       0.0000  (CFI=0.996,RMSEA= 0.085)
     Scalar            54           3159.482            122       0.0000  (CFI=0.996,RMSEA= 0.079)

but I got these from lavaan using measurementinavariance() :

Model 1: configural invariance:
   chisq       df          pvalue      cfi    rmsea 
1410.643   80.000    0.000    0.999    0.065 

Model 2: weak invariance (equal loadings):
   chisq       df          pvalue      cfi    rmsea 
1497.506  101.000    0.000    0.999    0.059

Model 3: strong invariance (equal loadings + intercepts):
   chisq       df         pvalue      cfi    rmsea 
1512.955  122.000    0.000    0.999    0.054 

As you can see chi-square estimates and fit measures are different. I tried test="Satorra.Bentler" but nothing changed.DFs for model comparisons are the same across software but again chi-squares are different.More specifically, chi-squares are increasing in lavaan but they have different pattern in Mplus.

What is the source of difference? Are the parameterizations different?Is it possible to produce the same results by lavaan?

Thanks,
Amin.

> 1512.955 122.000 0.000 0.999 0.054

Many things:

1) The measurementInvariance() function only works for continuous data!
(And yes, a warning should be in order).

2) If you have categorical indicators, you need to fit the
configural/metric/... models one by one, and use the lavTestLRT()
function to compare the models (the lavTestLRT() function is equivalent
to the anova() function, but has more options)

3) The intercepts are not used when you have categorical indicators.
Instead, you should constrain the thresholds to be equal

4) Even if you are using lavTestLRT(), the results are not the same as
if you were using DIFFTEST in Mplus. That is still a puzzle I need to
solve. lavaan uses the Satorra (2000) formulas. Mplus uses something
else (as usual). More news on this later.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Different measurement invariance results from lavaan and Mplus7
parts:
On 04/25/2014 05:07 PM, Amin Mousavi wrote:
> Hi Yves,
>
> Thanks.Which "test" option in cfa() can produce closer chi-square value
> to Mplus for categorical indicatros?

If you are using WLSMV (which is the default in both Mplus and lavaan
when data is categorical), then the default setting for the test
argument (test = "scaled.shifed") should reproduce the chi-square value
of Mplus very closely. If not, let me know.

The difference can only be seen if you are using DIFFTEST in Mplus, to
compare two nested models.

> Could you please give me a hint on how to set thresholds equal across
> groups?

The 'group.equal' argument can be used for this. For example, you can use

fit <- cfa(myModel, data=myData, group="Group",
group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"), ordered=c("i1","i2",...), ...)

Or, in the syntax, you can label the thresholds. If you want different
thresholds for each group, you give them a different label, eg

i1 | c(a1, a2)*t1

If you want to constrain the thresholds to be the same across groups,
you give them the same label:

i1 | c(a1,a1)*t1

Yves.

Hi Yves,

Following my previous question and our discussion, I ran a simple multigroup CFA using Mplus and lavaan.The data and Mplus output are attached.I used this codes for lavaan:

model<-'com=~q1+q2+q3+q4+q5+q6+q7+q8+q9'

m<-cfa(model,data=data,group="age",ordered=c("q1","q2","q3","q4","q5","q6","q7","q8","q9"),group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"))

I used group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds") because Mplus by default assumes that factor loadings and thresholds are equal across groups in multigroup CFA.If you take a look at the results you can see that they are different, specially overall Chi-square.
I also ran this model:

m1<-cfa(model,data=data,group="age",ordered=c("q1","q2","q3","q4","q5","q6","q7","q8","q9"))

using lavTestLRT() I got this:

Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (test = scaled.shifted)

     Df AIC BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
fa  108         1448.3                              
fa1 153         1557.5     48.692      45     0.3268

 lavTestLRT() is reporting normal theory chi-squares (i.e. 1448.3 & 1557) and not the scaled ones. I can see that Chisq-diff is scaled but since data are categorical it's supposed to report scaled chi-square. Additionally, DIFFTEST is showing significant difference between these two models (output is attached). In Mplus, I set some constrains to mimic lavaan specification for model m1.

I would be grateful to help me figure out this difference as I'm going to use lavaan for future works.Please let me know if I did something incorrectly.

Thanks,
Amin.

messages.subject: Re: Different measurement invariance results from lavaan and Mplus7
parts:
On 04/26/2014 07:28 AM, Amin Mousavi wrote:
> Hi Yves,
>
> Following my previous question and our discussion, I ran a simple
> multigroup CFA using Mplus and lavaan.The data and Mplus output are
> attached.I used this codes for lavaan:
>
> model<-'com=~q1+q2+q3+q4+q5+q6+q7+q8+q9'
>
> m<-cfa(model,data=data,group="age",ordered=c("q1","q2","q3","q4","q5","q6","q7","q8","q9"),group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"))
>
> I used *group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds")* because Mplus by default

> assumes that factor loadings and thresholds are equal across groups in
> multigroup CFA.

But your (restricted) Mplus model (see DIFFTEST.out) is a totally
different model. In your Mplus syntax, you have constrained the
thresholds, factor means, and scale factors to be equal across groups.
But NOT the loadings.

> using *lavTestLRT()* I got this:

>
> Scaled Chi Square Difference Test (test = scaled.shifted)
>
> Df AIC BIC Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)
> fa 108 1448.3
> fa1 153 1557.5 48.692 45 0.3268
>
> *lavTestLRT()* is reporting normal theory chi-squares (i.e. 1448.3 &
> 1557) and not the scaled ones.

The chi-squares or not normal theory based. But they are unscaled. That
is because we 'scale' the difference between the two unscaled chi-square
values in a scale chi-square difference test. See the Satorra (&
Bentler) papers describing these tests.

Yves.
